$comment: Draft from docs/portfolio.md, 'Contracts' (open decision 3 there: who the messaging owner is). The owner of the customer-insight card writes this file; adcut writes it today. The claims_scope object is the claims record kit/claimscope.py reads (subject, category, scope_text, allowed, source) with the fields of its confirmation, so the kit's compliance check can take it as it is once confirmed_on is left out (x-rules). Added on 2026-11-03, all optional, for the pack that will own the card: card_version, matrix, status and source of a row, the confirmation fields and lexicon_sha of the scope.
title: messages/1
description: What may be said, to whom: per segment, the pain, the objection and the facts that can be said about it, with the claims scope that bounds all copy for the product. The messaging owner writes it; makers, ad-copy, gads (search ad assets) and kos (creator briefs) read it. A matrix beside the sayable rows lists every row the owner holds, so a reader can place a creative or an ad on a row and can tell a dropped or held row from one that never existed.
x-rules: A document is for one product and one market.
Copy may name only what claims_scope.allowed names; a sayable fact is a fact the owner has confirmed, not a claim.
An absent optional key means unknown, never null and never an empty string.

A writer of words reads `insights` only: the matrix, a row's status and its tags are for placing, counting and asking, and the pain and the objection are the user's own situation, which may lie outside claims_scope.
An insight_id is never reused or renumbered for one product and market, whatever becomes of its row.

With a `matrix`, matrix.rows lists every id the producer has issued, a dropped one too (state dropped), and every id of `insights` is in it; an id in neither never existed. Without a `matrix`, an id missing from `insights` is not known to be missing: its row may be dropped, held or have nothing sayable yet.

may_say is true only for a live row that names a segment_id of the matrix whose segment has no hold and that says at least one fact (say_count above 0); exactly the rows with may_say true are in `insights`, and a dropped row is never in `insights`.

A pending scope is never acted on: while claims_scope.status is pending, `insights` is empty and no matrix row has may_say true; a reader that finds a sayable fact under a pending scope does not use it.

A scope is acted on only when claims_scope.status is confirmed. status is absent only in a document with neither card_version nor matrix (one written before 2026-11-03), and reads as confirmed there, because such a document was written only after a person confirmed the scope; a document with either carries status, and status confirmed comes with confirmed_by, confirmed_at and content_sha. A confirmation by an automatic mode is not a person's and is not written as confirmed.

A reader that must prove the confirmation hands claims_scope, without confirmed_on, to kit.claimscope.confirmed(): it is true only with status confirmed, confirmed_by, confirmed_at and a content_sha equal to the kit's hash of the object, so a scope written without them reads as a draft there. The hash shows that nobody changed the object after the producer wrote it; that a person confirmed the record is the word of the producer's own gate.

confirmed_on is the day part of confirmed_at as written, kept for readers that predate the confirmation fields; it is not part of the confirmed content, so content_sha is computed without it (lexicon_sha is part of what it covers).

producer.description: The pack that wrote the document (its CLI word).

produced_at.description: When the document was written: ISO 8601 with its zone.

product.description: The product the document is for: a sku of catalog/1 when there is one.

market.description: The market and language the words are for (the hub's market word).

card_version.description: The version of the producer's own record (the insight card) this document was built from; it goes up by 1 on every write of that record, so two documents of one product compare by it.

claims_scope.description: The wording that bounds all copy for the product: as a person approved it, or a draft while status is pending.

subject.description: The product, as the person retypes it at the gate.

category.description: The category word that picks the rules.

allowed.description: The canonical names of the claims that wording allows.

source.description: Where the wording was read (a photo, a page, a filing).

confirmed_on.description: The day a person confirmed the record, YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: confirmed: a person confirmed exactly this content (an automatic mode's confirmation is not a person's); pending: a draft that no copy may rest on; absent reads as confirmed only in a document with neither card_version nor matrix (x-rules).

confirmed_by.description: Who confirmed the record, as the producer's gate wrote it (the account and the channel the confirmation came through); written with status confirmed.

confirmed_at.description: When the record was confirmed: ISO 8601 with its zone.

content_sha.description: SHA-256 of this object as written, less confirmed_on and the confirmation's own fields, as kit.claimscope.content_sha computes it (lexicon_sha is in it), so a change made after the producer wrote it is seen.

lexicon_sha.description: SHA-256 of the claims lexicon file whose canonical names `allowed` holds, so a reader with another lexicon sees that the names may not mean the same.

insights.description: The rows that may be said now, one per segment and pain; empty when none can be said yet, and always while the scope is pending.

insight_id.description: Unique and stable, never reused or renumbered: a creative or an ad can name the insight it serves.

segment.description: Who this is for, in the client's words.

pain.description: What troubles them, in their words.

objection.description: What stops them buying, in their words.

sayable_facts.description: The facts that answer the pain or the objection and may be said, each one sentence.

status.description: Whether a person has answered this row, one of x-vocabulary.status (guess: nobody has; unchecked: the producer could not read the log of answers); a guess is a hypothesis.

source.description: What the row was written from, in the producer's words (a brief, a chat, a report).

matrix.description: Every row the producer holds, sayable or not, with the tags a reader places a creative or an ad by; `insights` is its sayable part.

segments.description: The segments the rows name, by id.

id.description: The segment's id, as rows[].segment_id names it.

name.description: Who the segment is, in the client's words (the segment of an insights row).

relation.description: How the buyer relates to the user, one of x-vocabulary.relation; absent when the segment does not say.

life_stage.description: The user's life stage when it matters to what may be said, one of x-vocabulary.life_stage.

hold.description: Present when a person put the segment on hold, one of x-vocabulary.hold: its rows are listed here and are not spoken to.

jobs.description: The jobs the rows name, by id.

id.description: The job's id, as rows[].job_id names it.

kind.description: What kind of job it is, one of x-vocabulary.job_kind.

moments.description: The moments of the buyer's journey the rows name, by id.

id.description: The moment's id, as rows[].moment_id names it.

stage.description: Where in the journey it falls, one of x-vocabulary.moment_stage.

kind.description: What kind of moment it is, one of x-vocabulary.moment_kind.

rows.description: One entry for every row the producer has issued for the product and market, a dropped one too, in the producer's order.

insight_id.description: The row's id, the same as in `insights`; never reused or renumbered.

state.description: live: the row stands; dropped: a person or the producer's agent lowered it, so nothing is made for it.

segment_id.description: The segment of the row: an id of matrix.segments.

job_id.description: The job the row is about: an id of matrix.jobs.

moment_id.description: The moment the row is about: an id of matrix.moments.

pain.description: What troubles them, in their words (internal: it may lie outside claims_scope and is never an ad's line).

objection.description: What stops them buying, in their words (internal, as pain).

status.description: Whether a person has answered this row, as insights[].status says.

may_say.description: True when the row is in `insights`: live, its segment without a hold, and at least one of its facts may be said now.

say_count.description: How many sayable facts the row names, whether or not they may be said yet; 0 means nothing is written for it.

ours_codes.description: The codes (ads.creatives/1) of our creatives that were made to serve the row.

flags.description: What the producer's own check found on the row that a person decides; empty or absent when nothing.

code.description: The producer's code for the finding, usually one of x-vocabulary.flag_code.

rule.description: The id of the rule that matched, in the producer's table of rules.

objections.description: The objections a coder may tag an ad with, one per distinct objection of the live rows, in row order; `none` (the ad answers no concern) and `other` are always allowed besides.

value.description: The tag value: the id of the first row that states the objection.

text.description: The objection in the rows' own words (internal, as pain).

rows.description: The ids of every row, a dropped one too, that states this objection, so a tag naming a later row reads as this value.
